column1: # CONTRACT-VERSIONS.tsv -- the version <-> contract-shape ledger (CONTRIBUTING rule 15).
# One row per APWORLD_VERSION, recording the CONTRACT_HASH that version ships.
# `tools/check_contract_version.py` reads this and goes RED when the contract has
# moved under a version number that did not.
# DERIVED, not hand-maintained. Every historical row below was computed by loading
# greenfield/eldenring/contract.py at that git tag and reading CONTRACT_HASH[:8]:
# 🛑 DO NOT EDIT AN EXISTING ROW TO MAKE THE GATE GREEN. That is falsifying history,
# and it is the one bypass this gate has. A contract change needs a NEW version and a
# NEW row. tests/test_gf_contract_versions.py pins these rows as a literal fixture, so
# editing one here reddens the suite as well.

Recorded here as its FINAL shape. A bug report saying "apworld/0.2.0" could mean any of the five.

v0.3.7 -- CONTRACT MOVED (SPEC-ashen-capital-lock, 2026-08-06): two new optional GREENFIELD keys, capitalWorldBurnFlag (300, the world's post-burn state -- without it the Elden Beast's arena is a void) and capitalPreBurnFlag (302, its opposite). First contract change since 0.3.0; every 0.3.x before this shared 5e8b11c9. Both are optional and independently absent-able, so a client that predates them still gets the burn via lockRevealFlags -- it latches the state instead of holding it by position.

v0.3.12 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. v0.4.0 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. Opened 2026-08-12 AT THE TAG of v0.3.12, the FIFTH window running opened on purpose rather than by a red gate -- except this one was NOT: main was red on check_release_notes (rule 14) from the moment the v0.3.12 tag was cut, and that red is what this window pays. 🛑 The MINOR component moves for the first time since 0.3.0, and it is not ceremony: under the 0.3.12 window `item_categories` reclassified 319 spells, spirit ashes and crystal tears from filler to useful, and useful is placed before filler -- the same yaml and the same seed number now produce a different layout. `rune_shop_pricing` also stopped being unconditional and became an option that is OFF by default, so a default seed no longer does something it did in 0.3.x. Two behaviour changes a player can see without reading a note is what a minor bump is for. The client half landed first (client PR #179); a gitlink can only point at a commit that exists.

v0.4.1 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. Opened 2026-08-13 minutes after the v0.4.0 tag at d9cdeafc, and NOT on purpose: commits had already landed past the tag. The first of them is the repair to `deploy_wizard.sh --landing`, which shipped in v0.4.0 writing to ${ER_ROOT_DIR}/index.html on the assumption that peliarch serves `/` from a static directory -- it does not, `/` is a Flask route, so that file would have been written, reported as installed, and never served. v0.4.2 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. Opened 2026-08-14 AT THE TAG of v0.4.1 at 07dea8d0, with ZERO commits past it, so nothing had to be moved out of a shipped section -- the cleanest open since v0.3.11. It is still not fully on purpose: v0.4.1 was tagged and `APWORLD_VERSION` was left naming it, so `check_release_notes` was already failing every PR opened past the tag (#647, whose content is comments only). 🛑 AND THE ABORT HID THE OTHER HALF AGAIN: rule 14 fails at step 9 of `generators`, so steps 10-12 were SKIPPED and `test_every_tagged_version_is_recorded_as_shipped` never ran to say v0.4.1's SHIPPED row was owed -- the same two-failures-in-line masking recorded at v0.3.12, now twice. The client half landed first (client PR #199); a gitlink can only point at a commit that exists.

v0.4.3 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. Opened 2026-08-15 AT THE TAG of v0.4.2 at 33c85f7, with ZERO commits past it. ⭐ THE FIRST WINDOW OPENED WHILE EVERY GATE WAS STILL GREEN: check_release_notes reported `HEAD is at the tag -- nothing has landed since` rather than failing, so this open was not paying a red, it was pre-empting the one the next commit past the tag would have caused. Every prior row from 0.3.10 on records the opposite. Two mechanisms that made previous opens expensive are also gone rather than paid: the SHIPPED fixture is DERIVED from `git tag` since #651, so v0.4.2's row cannot be owed and cannot be hidden behind rule 14's abort (the masking recorded at v0.3.12 and again at v0.4.2), and the gitlink rides in this branch rather than after it, which is what #648 got wrong and #650 repaired. The client half landed first (client PR: chore/open-v043-window-client); a gitlink can only point at a commit that exists.

v0.4.4 -- contract UNCHANGED from 0.3.9; version-lockstep for a new window. That row recorded the first window ever opened while every gate was still green, and predicted in its own words that the red would arrive on 'the first commit past it'. It did, on the next one. The pre-emptive open is still the better habit -- the cost here was one PR's CI and a blocked lane, not a shipped section accumulating notes that were never in the release, which is what the gate is actually there to prevent. The claim the rows MEAN is 'no CONTRACT KEY moved', which is true and is a different sentence. Client half: PR #246; gitlink bumped in this same commit per AGENTS 7. ⭐ THE COMPLETE SET OF SITES A WINDOW OPEN MOVES, measured here rather than remembered, because two of the seven were found by a red gate and not by the checklist: greenfield/eldenring/archipelago.json, greenfield/eldenring/contract.py, the client's Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock + contract_gen.rs (via the gitlink), and wizard/options-metadata.json + wizard/wizard.html -- the last two embed apworld_version and are regenerated with `tools/dump_options_metadata.py`, which the `tests` job checks with --check.
